s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness in a pediatric patient
key_facts: No recent infections or vaccinations beyond routine immunizations
No intracranial hemorrhage on head CT and brain MRI
Varix on the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) noted on brain MRI

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness in a pediatric patient
key_facts: No recent infections or vaccinations beyond routine immunizations
No intracranial hemorrhage on head CT and brain MRI
Varix on the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) noted on brain MRI

differentials: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy
Hereditary endotheliopathy with retinopathy, nephropathy, and stroke
Vasculitis of the central nervous system
Leukoencephalopathy with brainstem and spinal cord involvement and lactate elevation
Cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts
per_call: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy
Hereditary endotheliopathy with retinopathy, nephropathy, and stroke
Vasculitis of the central nervous system
Leukoencephalopathy with brainstem and spinal cord involvement and lactate elevation
Cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral weakness in a pediatric patient, with normal laboratory studies and no intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Varix on the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) noted on brain MRI, suggesting possible vascular anomaly

shortlist.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of neurological symptoms, with normal cerebrospinal fluid and no evidence of infection

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral weakness and headache, with normal laboratory studies and no evidence of infection or trauma

shortlist.label: Moyamoya syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Moyamoya disease, with possible underlying vascular anomaly

raw.rationale: The presence of a varix on the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) noted on brain MRI, in combination with the sudden onset of left-sided weakness and right-sided headache, suggests a vascular anomaly which is most consistent with an arteriovenous malformation.

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: Moyamoya disease typically presents with bilateral cerebral vasculopathy, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis is an inflammatory condition that would likely show abnormalities in cerebrospinal fluid or MRI findings consistent with demyelination, which are not present here.

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: Cerebral vasculitis would likely have other systemic symptoms or laboratory evidence of inflammation, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Moyamoya syndrome
rejected.why: Moyamoya syndrome refers to a condition with similar vasculopathy to Moyamoya disease but secondary to another condition; the primary condition is not identified in this case, making arteriovenous malformation a more direct explanation for the varix and symptoms.
